All sources used in this research, numbered sequentially. Each entry includes

**[1]** Sharma, M.; Tong, M.; Korbak, T. et al. "Towards Understanding
Sycophancy in Language Models." Anthropic / University of Toronto, 2023.
<https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13548>
**Tier:** 1
Data: Sycophancy defined as "model responses that match user beliefs over
truthful ones." Five state-of-the-art assistants tested across four tasks.
RLHF contributes by rewarding agreement. Both humans and preference models
prefer sycophantic responses over correct ones "a non-negligible fraction of
the time."

**[2]** Cheng, M.; Yu, S.; Lee, C.; Khadpe, P.; Ibrahim, L.; Jurafsky, D.
"ELEPHANT: Social Sycophancy Benchmark." Stanford University, 2025.
<https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13995>
**Tier:** 1
Data: LLMs preserve user's face 45 percentage points more than humans.
Dual-affirmation in moral conflicts: 48% of cases. 11 models tested.

**[3]** Mitropoulos, D.; Alexopoulos, N.; Alexopoulos, G.; Spinellis, D.
"Confirmation Bias in LLM Security Code Review." 2026.
<https://arxiv.org/html/2603.18740>
**Tier:** 1
Data: Bug-free framing reduced detection: GPT-4o-mini 97.2%→3.6% (93.5pp),
Claude 3.5 Haiku 68.4%→8.5%, DeepSeek V3 96.8%→53.8%, Gemini 2.0 Flash
95.5%→79.4%. All p<0.001. 250 CVE pairs, ~10,000 queries. Claude Code
adversarial success 88%.

**[4]** Lou, J. "Anchoring Bias in LLMs." National Day School, Beijing, 2024.
<https://arxiv.org/html/2412.06593v1>
**Tier:** 1
Data: Expert-opinion anchoring — zero exceptions across 12 questions. Average
anchoring index 0.45 for GPT-4 (vs 0.61 for humans). No simple mitigation
strategies effective for expert anchoring.

**[5]** Zhang, P.; Ye, Q.; Peng, Z.; Garimella, K.; Tyson, G. "Source

<https://arxiv.org/html/2512.09483>
**Tier:** 1
Data: 37% of LLM-SE domains absent from traditional SEs. LLM-SEs average 4.3
URLs per response vs 10.3. 55,936 queries, 124,287 unique domains. Gemini 41%
Wikipedia reliance.
